key_insight: LongMemEval-V2 (LME-V2) provides a focused benchmark that directly measures whether agent memory systems internalize environment-specific experience (interface affordances, workflows, failure modes) across long interactions, not just short traces or task success.
problem_solved: Existing memory benchmarks emphasize user histories or short-term performance and fail to evaluate whether agents retain and use nuanced, environment-specific experience over long horizons; LME-V2 fills this gap with tasks and metrics that probe true long-term, experience-driven memory.
method: Construct realistic web-style environments and repeated workflow episodes that produce rich, environment-specific experience traces (affordances, state dynamics, recurring failures).
Design targeted probe tasks and evaluation metrics that require recalling and applying past experiences after long time gaps (recall accuracy, retrieval utility, generalization to variant workflows).
Release a standardized dataset, evaluation protocol, and baseline results to compare memory architectures and retrieval strategies on long-term environment-specific retention.
impact: LME-V2 gives practitioners a practical, reproducible way to benchmark and improve long-term memory components in agents, enabling more reliable, adaptive behavior in specialized web and workflow-heavy settings.
visual_elements: Timeline diagram: agent experiences over time with markers for when memories are encoded and later probed
Architecture schematic: environment → agent → memory module → probe tasks, showing retrieval/usage loop

Heatmap: recall accuracy across different affordances, workflows, and recurring failure modes
paper_title: LongMemEval-V2: Evaluating Long-Term Agent Memory Toward Experienced Colleagues
paper_authors: Di Wu, Zixiang Ji, Asmi Kawatkar, Bryan Kwan, Jia-Chen Gu
